tasks.short: Read the referral and record, assess nutritional needs with the patient, calculate energy and protein needs, develop the dietary-care plan, counsel the patient, and write the consult note and plan.

steps.what: Dietitian reads the referral, diet restrictions and current health plans in the record
Dietitian assesses nutritional needs and eating habits with the patient
Dietitian calculates energy and protein needs in a spreadsheet
Dietitian develops the dietary-care plan
Dietitian provides nutritional counseling on the plan
Dietitian writes the consult note and care plan in the record

loop.input: The recorded consultation, with the patient's consent, and the calculated needs.
loop.output: A draft consult note and care plan in the record's format.
loop.check: Code checks every number in the draft (energy, protein, weight) against the calculation and record values and flags mismatches; the dietitian edits and approves before the note is saved.
loop.stop: One draft per consult; if the patient declines recording or the dietitian rejects the draft, the dietitian writes the note.
loop.why_not_simpler: The conversation covers habits and preferences in free speech; a form cannot capture them.

tasks.design: The record ({OTHER}) shows weight trend, relevant lab values, allergies, medication and the referral question in one nutrition view. Energy and protein needs are calculated by fixed formulas in the record from weight, height and activity level, instead of a spreadsheet. With the patient's consent, a scribe drafts the consult note from the conversation; code checks every number against the record, and the dietitian edits and approves before it is saved. Assessing, planning and counselling stay with the dietitian.
tasks.previous_blocker: Data were gathered from several screens, needs calculated in spreadsheets and notes typed after the consult.
tasks.enabler_now: Records show nutrition views; scribes draft notes that the clinician validates.
tasks.human_edge: Finding the one change a patient will keep.
tasks.altitude: The dietitian validates notes instead of typing them.

reach.learn: Whether nutrition plans are in the record on the day.

evidence.claim: Autoscriber records the consultation and the clinician validates the note before it goes into the record.
At Capio Ramsay Santé, 1,295 clinicians reported time per note falling from 6.69 to 4.72 minutes with Tandem notes; three of seven authors were from the vendor.
Ambient recording captures staff performance and needs works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the referral to the note recorded; follow-up consults are outside.
Input contract: lab values and weights in the record; fallback is reading screens and typing.
A DPIA and works council consent come before recording.
research_questions: How long does the dietitian spend editing drafted notes?

already_counted.description: Dietitian edits and approves drafted notes.

incremental.description: Dietitian asks each patient's consent for recording.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: short follow-ups; high: long first consults with complex records.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Look up lab results, track trends, evaluate the tests against the patient's condition, write nutrition recommendations, and discuss them with the physician.

steps.what: Dietitian looks up laboratory test results across record screens
Dietitian copies values into a spreadsheet to track trends
Dietitian evaluates laboratory tests against the patient's condition
Dietitian writes nutrition recommendations in the record
Dietitian discusses the recommendations with the treating physician

tasks.design: A nutrition lab panel in the record ({OTHER}) shows albumin, glucose, kidney function, electrolytes and vitamin levels with trend lines, so the dietitian does not search screens or copy values into a spreadsheet. The recommendation template pulls in the latest values. Evaluating the tests, writing the advice and agreeing it with the physician stay with the dietitian.
tasks.previous_blocker: Lab values were spread over screens and trends kept in spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Records can show lab panels with trend lines.
tasks.still_hard: Lab values reflect illness as much as nutrition.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that low albumin here means inflammation, not poor intake.

reach.learn: Whether nutrition advice cites current values.

evidence.claim: Records can show lab panels with trend lines and fill templates with the latest values.
The dossier is kept twenty years after the last change.

assumptions: Boundary: from the referral to recommendations agreed; treatment changes are outside.
Input contract: lab results in the hospital record; fallback is searching screens.
Evaluating tests stays with the dietitian.
unknowns: Patients with lab review per day.
research_questions: Do recommendations reach the record sooner?

incremental.description: Dietitian adds lab values from outside labs by hand.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few lab values; high: long stays with many lab results.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Counsel individuals and groups on good nutrition and healthy eating habits, prepare handouts, draft replies to follow-up questions, and send them.

steps.what: Dietitian counsels individuals on good nutrition and healthy eating habits
Dietitian prepares handouts and session materials on nutrition monitoring
Dietitian leads group sessions on healthy eating
Dietitian writes replies to follow-up questions about nutrition

loop.input: The patient's question and the practice's vetted patient information texts.
loop.output: A draft reply quoting the vetted texts.
loop.check: Every advice sentence must cite a paragraph from the vetted texts or it is dropped; questions about symptoms or medication are not drafted; the dietitian edits and approves every reply.
loop.stop: One draft per question; if no sentence passes, the dietitian writes the reply.
loop.why_not_simpler: Patients ask in their own words; a fixed list of answers does not match their questions.

steps.what: Dietitian e-mails the reply to the patient

tasks.design: Handouts come from a shared library of vetted, guideline-based patient texts ({DOCS}) that the dietitian adapts instead of writing new ones. For follow-up questions, a bounded step drafts a reply only from those texts; every advice sentence must cite a paragraph, symptom and medication questions go straight to the dietitian, and the dietitian approves every reply before it is sent through the patient portal. Counselling individuals and groups stays with the dietitian.
tasks.previous_blocker: Handouts and replies were written by each dietitian.
tasks.enabler_now: Vetted patient texts exist; language models draft replies that cite them.
tasks.still_hard: Advice must fit the patient's culture and budget.
tasks.human_edge: Getting a group to share what they really eat.
tasks.altitude: The dietitian approves replies instead of writing each one.

evidence.claim: Thuisarts publishes guideline-based patient information made by NHG, FMS and Patiëntenfederatie.
Providers are legally responsible for careful use of generative AI: assess risks, train, test and monitor after updates.

assumptions: Boundary: from the counselling request to the reply sent; medical treatment is outside.
Input contract: vetted texts kept by the practice; fallback is writing by hand.
Patients read replies as before; no added patient time.
research_questions: How many drafted replies does the dietitian change?

incremental.description: Dietitian keeps the vetted text library current.

approvals.approved_version: The reply as edited and approved by the dietitian in s4.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few follow-up questions; high: many group participants with questions.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Advise patients and families on diet modifications in the consultation, draft a personal meal plan with food selection and preparation tips, check it, send it, and answer families' calls.

steps.what: Dietitian advises patients and their families on nutritional principles and diet modifications
Dietitian writes a personal meal plan with food selection and preparation tips

loop.input: The dietary plan (energy, protein, restrictions), the patient's food preferences and a food composition table.
loop.output: A draft week meal plan with recipes and preparation tips.
loop.check: Code computes the nutrients of the drafted plan from the food composition table and rejects plans outside the targets or containing restricted foods; the dietitian edits.
loop.stop: Up to three redrafts; if none passes, the dietitian writes the plan.
loop.why_not_simpler: Patients keep to meals they like; a fixed menu does not fit their habits and kitchen.

steps.what: Dietitian checks the final meal plan
Dietitian e-mails the meal plan to the patient
Dietitian answers families' calls on food preparation

tasks.design: After the consultation, a bounded step drafts a week meal plan from the dietary plan, the patient's preferences and a food composition table; code computes the nutrients of the draft and rejects plans outside the targets or containing restricted foods. The dietitian edits and checks the plan, and once checked it goes to the patient through the patient portal. Advising patients and families and answering their calls stay with the dietitian.
tasks.previous_blocker: Meal plans were written and checked against nutrient targets by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Language models draft meal plans; food composition tables let code check nutrients.
tasks.still_hard: Families cook for several people with different needs.
tasks.human_edge: Adapting a diet to a family's culture and budget.
tasks.altitude: The dietitian edits checked drafts instead of writing plans from scratch.

reach.learn: Whether plans are followed at home.

evidence.claim: Language models can draft meal plans; nutrients can be computed by code from a food composition table.
Health data are special category data; expect a DPIA.

assumptions: Boundary: from the dietary plan to calls answered; follow-up consults are outside.
Input contract: food composition table loaded; fallback is writing plans by hand.
Families read the plan as before; no added family time.
research_questions: Do patients keep to drafted plans as well as to hand-written ones?

incremental.description: Dietitian adds recipes the patient asks for to the plan library.

approvals.approved_version: The meal plan as checked by the dietitian in s3.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: simple diets; high: complex diets with many restrictions.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The dietitian keeps assessing, planning, evaluating lab tests and counselling; screen searching, spreadsheet calculations, typed notes and hand-written meal plans shrink.
skills_to_grow: Checking drafted notes and meal plans
role.ambitious_version: A dietitian with more time for counselling.
